abstract.t: This document defines EBGP-OAD, a form of External BGP (EBGP) peering used between two EBGP peers that belong to One Administrative Domain (OAD), in which explicit policy configuration allows the behavior of certain path attributes to differ from the EBGP default.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: At each EBGP boundary, BGP path attributes are modified as per , which includes stripping any attributes not allowed over an EBGP session. An example is the LOCAL_PREF attribute.

Some networks span more than one autonomous system and require more flexibility in the propagation of path attributes. It is worth noting that these multi-AS networks have a common or single administrative entity. These networks are said to belong to One Administrative Domain (OAD). It is desirable to have the ability to carry any attribute across EBGP peerings when the peers belong to an OAD.

This document defines EBGP-OAD, a form of EBGP peering used between two EBGP peers that belong to an OAD. EBGP-OAD is not a peering type distinct from EBGP; rather, it is an EBGP session for which explicit policy configuration allows the behavior of certain path attributes (described in ) to differ from the EBGP default. This document also defines rules for route announcement and processing for EBGP-OAD peers.

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

section.name: Discussion
section.t: Networks have traditionally been demarcated by an autonomous system/BGP border, which correlates to an administrative boundary. This paradigm no longer serves the needs of network designers or customers due to the decoupling of the Interior Gateway Protocol (IGP) from BGP, BGP-free core in the underlay (e.g., using BGP labeled unicast ), the use of BGP to facilitate multiple service overlays (e.g., L2VPN, L3VPN, etc.) spanning multiple regions and AS domains, and the instantiation of customer sites on multiple content service providers (CSPs).

For example, an enterprise customer's sites, connected via a BGP/MPLS VPN operated by a third-party network provider, may themselves be distributed across different AS domains that are all under the customer's own administration (i.e., the customer's sites form an OAD). In such cases, the customer may want certain attributes relevant to their own VPN routes to be propagated consistently among all of their sites, to influence the BGP decision process at each site.

section.name: Operation
section.t: defines two types of BGP peerings used during a BGP protocol session: EBGP and IBGP. This document does not define a third peering type. Instead, it defines EBGP-OAD, which is an EBGP session between peers in different Autonomous Systems that belong to an OAD. By default, EBGP-OAD peers follow the EBGP route advertisement, route processing, path attribute announcement, and processing rules as defined in ; explicit policy configuration MAY enable the behavior of certain path attributes, described in the following subsections, to differ from that default.
EBGP-OAD peers handle receiving optional transitive attributes as specified in . Unrecognized non-transitive optional attributes MUST be quietly ignored and not passed along to other BGP peers.
Unless explicitly specifed, EBGP-OAD speakers are allowed to announce and receive any attribute over an EBGP-OAD session. Receiving any attribute over an EBGP-OAD session MUST NOT result in an error.

EBGP-OAD sessions MUST comply with the behavior specified in . Furthermore, the propagation of attributes not allowed over EBGP sessions (see ) MUST be explicitly allowed by an Export Policy, and their reception SHOULD be explicitly allowed by an Import Policy.
An EBGP-OAD speaker MUST support four-octet AS numbers and advertise the "support for four-octet AS number capability" .

This section addresses only the path attributes defined at the time of this writing, which are not marked as "deprecated" in the "BGP Path Attributes" registry , whose behavior over an EBGP-OAD session differs from standard EBGP behavior. All other path attributes not listed in this section MUST follow standard EBGP behavior as specified in or in the document in which they are defined. summarizes the behavior for EBGP, IBGP, and EBGP-OAD peerings.
Documents specifying new path attributes MUST indicate whether they are allowed for EBGP, IBGP, and EBGP-OAD peerings.

section.name: NEXT_HOP
section.t: The NEXT_HOP attribute is a well-known mandatory BGP path attribute that SHOULD be present in UPDATE messages sent over EBGP-OAD sessions . The origination and modification of the NEXT_HOP attribute MUST comply with the EBGP-related specification in .
It is reasonable for members of an OAD to share a common reachability domain. In such a case, the NEXT_HOP attribute MAY be left unchanged.

section.name: MULTI_EXIT_DISC
section.t: The MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute is an optional non-transitive BGP path attribute that MAY be present in UPDATE messages sent over EBGP-OAD sessions, even if it has been received from a neighboring AS. Otherwise, the use of the MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute MUST comply with the specification in .

The determination of the neighboring AS for the purpose of BGP Route Selection MAY ignore the ASNs of other members of the OAD. If so, all the members of the OAD SHOULD be configured to use the same criteria. Failure to do so may result in inconsistent forwarding between members of the OAD. Care should also be taken to avoid the creation of persistent route oscillations, similar to the Type II Churn described in . provides solutions and recommendations to address this issue.

section.name: LOCAL_PREF
section.t: The LOCAL_PREF attribute is a well-known BGP path attribute that MAY be present in UPDATE messages sent over EBGP-OAD sessions. The use of the LOCAL_PREF attribute MUST comply with the specification in .

section.name: COMMUNITIES
section.t: The COMMUNITIES attribute is an optional transitive BGP path attribute that MAY be present in UPDATE messages sent over EBGP-OAD sessions. The advertisement semantics MUST comply with the specification in .

Routes with a COMMUNITIES attribute containing the well-known NO_EXPORT community SHOULD NOT be advertised across an EBGP-OAD session unless allowed by explicit policy configuration. If allowed, all the members of the OAD SHOULD be configured to use the same criteria. Failure to do so may result in inconsistent forwarding between members of the OAD.
Routes with a COMMUNITIES attribute containing the well-known NO_EXPORT_SUBCONFED community MUST NOT be advertised across an EBGP-OAD session.

section.name: ORIGINATOR_ID
section.t: The ORIGINATOR_ID attribute is an optional non-transitive BGP path attribute . By default, it MUST NOT be advertised over an EBGP-OAD session. If received from an EBGP-OAD neighbor, it SHALL be discarded using the "attribute discard" approach . An implementation MAY log an error message for further analysis.
The ORIGINATOR_ID attribute MAY be exchanged over an EBGP-OAD session if allowed by explicit policy configuration.

section.name: CLUSTER_LIST
section.t: The CLUSTER_LIST attribute is an optional non-transitive BGP path attribute . By default, it MUST NOT be advertised over an EBGP-OAD session. If received from an EBGP-OAD neighbor, it SHALL be discarded using the "attribute discard" approach . An implementation MAY log an error message for further analysis.
The CLUSTER_LIST attribute MAY be exchanged over an EBGP-OAD session if allowed by explicit policy configuration.

section.name: MP_REACH_NLRI
section.t: The MP_REACH_NLRI attribute is an optional non-transitive BGP path attribute . The use of the MP_REACH_NLRI attribute MUST comply with the EBGP-related specification in .
It is reasonable for members of an OAD to share a common reachability domain. In such a case, the Next Hop in the MP_REACH_NLRI attribute MAY be left unchanged.

section.name: EXTENDED COMMUNITIES
section.t: The EXTENDED COMMUNITIES attribute is a transitive optional BGP path attribute that MAY be advertised over an EBGP-OAD session.

Extended communities which are non-transitive across an AS boundary MAY be advertised over an EBGP-OAD session if allowed by explicit policy configuration. For example, the Origin Validation State Extended Community, defined as non-transitive in , can be advertised to peers in the same OAD.

section.name: IPv6 Address Specific Extended Community
section.t: The IPv6 Address Specific Extended Community attribute is an optional transitive BGP path attribute that MAY be advertised over an EBGP-OAD session.
Extended communities which are non-transitive across Autonomous Systems MAY be advertised over an EBGP-OAD session if allowed by explicit policy configuration.

section.name: AIGP
section.t: The AIGP attribute is an optional non-transitive BGP path attribute that MAY be advertised over an EBGP-OAD session. The default value of AIGP_SESSION MUST be "disabled" and it MAY be "enabled" by explicit policy configuration. The use of the AIGP attribute MUST comply with the specification in .

section.name: BGP-LS Attribute
section.t: The BGP Link-State (BGP-LS) attribute is an optional non-transitive BGP path attribute that MAY be advertised over an EBGP-OAD session. The use of the BGP-LS Attribute MUST comply with the specification in .

section.name: BGP Community Container
section.t: The BGP Community Container attribute is an optional transitive BGP path attribute that MAY be advertised over an EBGP-OAD session.

In particular, communities with the T bit not set MAY be advertised over an EBGP-OAD session if allowed by explicit policy configuration. Communities with the T bit set MUST be advertised over an EBGP-OAD session. Communities with the C bit not set MUST NOT be advertised over an EBGP-OAD session. Communities with the C bit set MAY be advertised over an EBGP-OAD session if allowed by explicit policy configuration. In all cases, all the members of the OAD SHOULD be configured to use the same criteria.

section.name: Only to Customer
section.t: The Only to Customer (OTC) attribute is an optional transitive BGP path attribute that MAY be advertised over an EBGP-OAD session. However, the BGP Role negotiation and OTC Attribute-based procedures specified in are NOT RECOMMENDED to be used between peers using an EBGP-OAD session. If received, the OTC attribute MUST be preserved unchanged. The use and negotiation of BGP Roles between EBGP-OAD peers is outside the scope of this document.

section.name: Operational Considerations
section.t: For the Import and Export Policies to behave as expected, both EBGP-OAD speakers must be configured to use EBGP-OAD. If only one BGP speaker is so configured, and the other uses a plain EBGP session, the result is that some path attributes may be ignored and others will be discarded.

By default, a BGP session between different autonomous systems SHOULD be a plain EBGP session. A BGP implementation SHOULD provide a configuration-time option to enable EBGP-OAD on a given session. Whether a session is configured as a plain EBGP session or as EBGP-OAD may be changed without restarting the BGP session, since EBGP-OAD is, by default, the same as EBGP; the change only affects how path attributes are subsequently processed.

If multiple peerings exist between autonomous systems that belong to an OAD, all SHOULD be configured consistently. Improper configuration may result in inconsistent or unexpected forwarding. The inconsistent use of EBGP-OAD sessions is out of scope of this document.
BGP Confederations provide similar behavior, on a session by session basis, as what is specified in this document. The use of confederations with an EBGP-OAD peering is out of scope of this document.

requires that the BGP Identifier of a BGP speaker be unique within a single Autonomous System. In case of OAD, all the interconnected OAD members are considered as one AS for the purpose of supporting the AS-wide Unique BGP Identifier.

Because EBGP-OAD is a form of EBGP session, routes received over an EBGP-OAD session are treated as EBGP routes for the purposes of the BGP Decision Process , and are therefore preferred over routes received via IBGP. Operators wishing to influence this preference (e.g., to prefer an IBGP-learned route over one received via EBGP-OAD) can use existing BGP mechanisms such as LOCAL_PREF.

Members of an OAD may use a locally-defined community to indicate that a route musto not be advertised across an EBGP-OAD session. In general, this type of community only controls the propagation of the route it is attached to. It does not affect the propagation of individual path attributes, which continues to be governed by Import/Export Policy configuration. In particular, an attribute added to the route after the community was set (for example, by an intervening EBGP-OAD peering) is not covered by this community and remains subject to explicit policy configuration.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: EBGP-OAD peering does not change the underlying security issues inherent in the existing BGP protocol, such as those described in and . Any security considerations related to existing path attributes apply to EBGP-OAD sessions.

All BGP attributes may now be propagated to another autonomous system. However, it is expected that EBGP-OAD will only be enabled when peering with a router that also belongs to the OAD. If misconfigured, the impact is minimal due to the fact that both and define mechanisms to deal with unexpected path attributes. Also, the use of the Import and Export Policy mechanisms speficied in are REQUIRED.
